title: Lab 3 — Quiz 2
subtitle: Bacterial Growth — TSI, phenol red fermentation, probiotic counts

questions.prompt: In fermentation, what is the purpose of Step 2 (reducing pyruvate)?

options.text: To regenerate NAD so glycolysis can continue
To generate most of the cell's ATP
To consume oxygen as the final electron acceptor

questions.explanation: Step 1 (glycolysis) oxidizes glucose and nets 2 ATP. Step 2 reduces pyruvate to acid or alcohol, regenerating NAD.

questions.prompt: The acidity of yogurt, sour cream and sourdough comes from:
questions.explanation: Lactic acid fermentation (pyruvate reduced to lactic acid) makes yogurt, sour cream and sourdough acidic, and happens in muscles when O2 runs out.

why.A: Ethanol fermentation produces alcohol and CO2.
why.B: H2S is the sulfur result in TSI.
why.C: These foods are acidified by lactic acid fermentation.

questions.prompt: In the probiotic experiment, 100 µL is transferred into 900 µL of water at each step (OG → A → B → C → D). What is the total dilution of Tube D?

why.B: Dilution factors are multiplied, not added.
why.D: Only four 1/10 dilutions were made: A, B, C, D.

questions.prompt: Plate D (total dilution 1/10,000, 50 µL plated) has 45 colonies. How many CFU/mL were in the probiotic?

why.A: That forgets to divide by the 0.05 mL plated.
why.C: Volume plated goes in the denominator: 45 × 10,000 ÷ 0.05.

questions.prompt: On this mannitol salt agar plate, the medium turned yellow. What does phenol red tell you?
questions.explanation: Phenol red is the pH indicator in MSA: yellow = acid from mannitol fermentation.

why.B: Growth on MSA means it IS salt-tolerant.

questions.prompt: What are the end products of ethanol (alcoholic) fermentation?
questions.explanation: Ethanol fermentation: pyruvate is reduced to ethanol, releasing CO2, and NAD is regenerated.

questions.prompt: Which pathway occurs in animal muscles when oxygen is depleted?
questions.explanation: Lactic acid fermentation is common in prokaryotes and eukaryotes, and occurs in muscle when O2 is depleted.

why.A: Ethanol fermentation is done by organisms like yeast.
why.C: This happens when O2 runs out.

questions.prompt: In lactic acid fermentation of lactose, what happens first?

options.text: Lactose is reduced directly to lactic acid
Lactose is converted into ethanol and CO2
Lactose is oxidized in the Krebs cycle
Lactose is broken into galactose and glucose

questions.explanation: Lactose → galactose + glucose; glucose enters glycolysis; pyruvate is reduced to lactic acid.

why.A: Lactose is split first; glucose then enters glycolysis.
why.C: Fermentation uses glycolysis, not the Krebs cycle.

questions.prompt: How many ATP (net) does fermentation produce per glucose?
questions.explanation: Step 1 (glycolysis) oxidizes glucose and nets 2 ATP; Step 2 only regenerates NAD.

why.C: Step 2 regenerates NAD; it makes no ATP.

questions.prompt: Bread rising and alcoholic beverages are products of which microbe's fermentation?
questions.explanation: Saccharomyces (brewer's/baker's yeast) ferments sugars to ethanol and CO2 — the CO2 makes bread rise.

options.text: A drug that kills harmful bacteria
Live beneficial microbes taken to support health
A dead vaccine that protects the gut
A medium used to count bacteria

questions.explanation: Probiotics are live microorganisms (often lactic acid bacteria) that benefit the host; in lab you counted the live bacteria in one.

questions.prompt: Why was a plate count (not turbidity) used to measure the bacteria in the probiotic?

options.text: Turbidity counts only the live cells
Turbidity is more accurate for probiotics

questions.explanation: Only live cells form colonies (CFUs); a probiotic's label claims live cells.

why.A: Turbidity counts live AND dead cells.
why.B: Turbidity counts total cells, including dead ones.
why.C: Serial dilutions were used in the experiment.

questions.prompt: In fermentation, NAD is regenerated when:

options.text: ATP is made by the electron transport chain

questions.explanation: Step 2 passes electrons from NADH to pyruvate, regenerating NAD so glycolysis can continue.

why.A: Step 1 uses NAD and makes NADH.

questions.prompt: Phenol red is used in mannitol salt agar because it is a pH indicator that turns:
questions.explanation: Phenol red: yellow = acidic, red-orange = neutral, pink = basic.

questions.prompt: Compare the two major fermentation pathways: what does Step 2 produce in each?

options.text: Acidic: ethanol + CO2; alcoholic: lactic acid
Acidic: lactic acid; alcoholic: ethanol + CO2
Both produce ATP through an electron transport chain

questions.explanation: Both pathways share glycolysis (Step 1); in Step 2 pyruvate is reduced to an acid (lactic) or to alcohol (ethanol + CO2), regenerating NAD.

why.C: Alcoholic fermentation makes ethanol and CO2.
why.D: Fermentation's ATP comes only from glycolysis.
